moduleTitle: Mastering advanced editing techniques in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Perform advanced editing on tests using keyboard shortcuts, or by passing information into a test step through parameters.
Demonstrate the process of copying values directly from the web or mobile application to be used in later test steps.
Synchronize tests with application behavior by waiting for specific events like element visibility, text display, or file downloads.

elements.description: Add Keyboard Shortcut sends a supported combination to the AUT. Windows/Mac fields synchronize equivalent shortcuts by default; Unsync Fields permits separate combinations. Inspect the effective test configuration OS rather than assuming the host OS always wins.

In Properties, press the combination in the applicable Windows or Mac field. The opposite field receives the default translation; use Unsync Fields when the intended combinations differ. A conflicting test-configuration OS governs which command is sent.
Unsupported combinations produce an unsupported keyboard shortcut error. Inspect failure handling rather than inferring that the entire test must always stop or always continue.

bulletPoints: Add Keyboard Shortcut step sends a key combo to the AUT — an Actions-menu predefined step.
Default field synchronization translates shortcuts; Unsync Fields and effective OS configuration matter.
An unrecognized combination throws an explicit 'unsupported keyboard shortcut' error.

elements.description: Parameters let a step or group be customized per use — passing in different information without knowing every value in advance — so the same underlying steps serve multiple scenarios instead of being copy-pasted with small edits each time.

Before execution, config-file values override params-file values, which override default test/run data; beforeTest overrides beforeSuite within the config file. During execution, scope and later assignments matter: a more local same-name parameter can shadow a broader one. This is not a universal parameters-always-win rule.

bulletPoints: Parameters pass custom information into a step/group instead of hardcoding it.
Distinguish pre-run source precedence from runtime scope and later assignments.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Extract Value: capturing data for later steps

elements.description: Extract Value captures selected AUT element text. Extract Mode chooses the whole text or number/date/Regex matches; individual matches remain strings and all-matches modes can return arrays. Selecting a mode does not guarantee a JavaScript number/date type.

elements.text: Email/SMS retrieval uses its own supported message workflow. Extract Value is not a universal connector to every source. Keep message/content assertions separate from extracting one useful value.

bulletPoints: Capture selected element text and choose the required Extract Mode.
Treat match selection and JavaScript value type separately.
Use the appropriate source retrieval and outcome assertions.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Wait for Events: synchronizing tests with the application

elements.term: Waiting for an event, not a fixed time
elements.description: Use the supported wait for readiness such as element visibility, text or a completed download, with a bounded step timeout. Wait for Download uses the documented scripted completion check; adding the step alone does not configure every possible file condition.

elements.term: Wait for element visible / not visible
elements.description: Visible waiting is available for web and mobile; documented not-visible waiting is web-only. Prepare the relevant AUT state before targeting. Visibility is not merely DOM presence, and absence from view does not necessarily mean removal.

elements.term: Changing the element after the fact
elements.description: Use Reassign when the required target is different. If the same element still exists with changed identification, consider Improve. Validate the wait condition and timeout; extending time alone does not fix a wrong target.

bulletPoints: Waitable events include element visibility, text display, and file downloads — not just a fixed duration.
Wait for element visible / not visible are added like any other predefined step, then targeted at an element.
To retarget a wait step's element, use Properties → Reassign — the same mechanism as any other step, not re-recording.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming an unrecognized keyboard shortcut fails silently or gracefully degrades
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Expecting Testim to ignore an unsupported key combination and continue the test, or to substitute the closest supported shortcut.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Unsupported combinations report an error; verify supported shortcuts and effective OS configuration. Run-level handling depends on the applicable failure settings.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming test data always wins over parameters
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Defining both a parameter and matching test data for the same field and expecting the test data value to be used.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Apply the documented pre-run chain for a matching value: config file > params file > default test/run data. During execution, inspect scope and later assignments instead of assuming all parameters always win.

examPitfalls.title: Re-recording a Wait for element visible step just to point it at a different element
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Deleting and re-recording a wait step from scratch because the wrong element was targeted.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Open the step's Properties and use Reassign to point it at the correct element — the same target-element mechanism used on any other step, no re-recording required.

examPitfalls.title: Extracting an entire block of text instead of the specific value needed
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Capturing a whole confirmation message or email body with Extract Value, then trying to parse it in a later step.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use a suitable extraction match and validate the captured type/value. Retrieval from email/SMS and asserting message correctness are separate tasks.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How does Testim react if you use a keyboard shortcut that it does not recognize?

options.text: Testim will show an error saying unsupported keyboard shortcut.
Testim defaults to the closest equivalent keyboard shortcut.
Testim will add the keyboard shortcut step to the test case but will not let you run the test.
Testim will ignore the unrecognized keyboard shortcut and continue the test execution.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's an explicit, named error — not a silent fallback.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The shortcut documentation specifies an unsupported keyboard shortcut error. It does not describe automatic nearest-equivalent substitution or silent ignoring; downstream failure behavior depends on configuration.

optionExplanations.A: The supported-shortcut guide documents this error.
optionExplanations.B: Unsupported combinations are not automatically replaced by the nearest shortcut.
optionExplanations.C: This is not the documented error behavior.
optionExplanations.D: Unsupported input is not documented as silently ignored.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Before execution, default test data and a params-file entry define the same parameter, with no config-file override. Which source wins under the documented rule?

options.text: The params-file value overrides the default test data value.
Default test data overrides the params-file value.
The value is selected randomly on each run.
Both values are always discarded.

practiceQuiz.hint: Use the documented pre-run source precedence, not a universal runtime claim.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Before execution, params-file values override default test/run data; config-file values would take precedence over the params file. Runtime scope and later assignment rules are distinct.

optionExplanations.A: The params-file source overrides matching default test data before execution.
optionExplanations.B: This reverses the documented pre-run rule.
optionExplanations.C: Precedence is defined rather than random.
optionExplanations.D: Matching definitions are resolved by precedence, not automatically discarded.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How do you select which text or matches an Extract Value step captures from an AUT element?

options.text: The user can enter the extract value step properties and set the extract mode.
The user can specify the data type when writing the code for the step.
The user can navigate to the Project Settings panel and set the required data type.
The step can capture only the entire text and cannot select matches.

practiceQuiz.hint: Extract Mode selects matches; this is distinct from the resulting JavaScript type.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Choose Extract Mode in the step’s Properties. Number/date/Regex modes select matches, whose individual values remain strings; all-matches modes support arrays. This setting is not a project-wide datatype switch.

optionExplanations.A: Extract Mode selects the whole text or required matches.
optionExplanations.B: Code is not required to choose the step’s built-in extraction mode.
optionExplanations.C: Extraction mode is configured per step, not globally in the project.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Wait for element visible step must target a different control. How can you change its target without recreating the step?

options.text: Go to the "Properties" menu and reassign a different element.
Delete the current step and re-record it with the new element.
Change the wait duration to allow more time for the element to appear.
Access the main menu and choose a different wait option.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's the same target-element mechanism used everywhere else in Testim.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Open Properties and Reassign the different target. If identification of the same target changed instead, Improve can be relevant; a longer wait does not select a different control.

optionExplanations.A: Reassign selects the required different target.
optionExplanations.B: The existing target can be changed without recreating the step.
optionExplanations.C: Longer timing does not select a different control.
optionExplanations.D: A different wait type does not by itself assign this required target.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Besides waiting for an element to become visible, which of the following is also something Testim's Wait for Events functionality can synchronize a test against?

options.text: A file finishing its download.
The tester's mouse movement speed.
The number of open browser tabs.
The project's billing plan tier.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think application-behavior events: visibility, text, and this one.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The documented Wait for Download workflow checks download completion before continuing, with suitable configuration and timeout. Mouse speed, billing and tab count are not the listed built-in completion events; custom logic is a separate mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: The documented download workflow can wait for file completion.
optionExplanations.B: Mouse movement speed is not the listed download/visibility/text readiness event.
optionExplanations.C: Tab count is not one of these built-in readiness events.
optionExplanations.D: Billing tier is not an application completion event.

quickRecap.value: Windows/Mac shortcut fields synchronize by default; Unsync Fields and configuration OS affect the sent command.
Pre-run: config file > params file > default data. Runtime scope and later assignments also matter.
Choose whole text or matches in Properties; individual matches remain strings, all-matches can return arrays.
Wait for supported readiness with a timeout; configure download completion checks explicitly.
Properties → Reassign, same as any other step — no re-recording needed.
